instrument_or_setup.value: EMPYREAN, PANALYTICAL diffractometer with Co-Kα source (operating voltage 40 kV; operating current 40 mA); scan rate 5° min⁻¹

key_findings.value: The diffraction peak intensity of all elements decreases with milling time; low-intensity peaks of all elements vanish after 5 h of milling; the intensity of the Al peak diminishes after 15 h of milling, indicating Al has the highest alloying rate; the BCC and γ-brass-type solid-solution phases form only after 25 h of milling.

measurement_conditions.value: Milled powder at various milling times; patterns recorded at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 h (the 15 h pattern is part of this series)

purpose.value: To study the alloying behavior and phase evolution of the powder during mechanical milling

source.reason: XRD is the technique used to follow phase evolution of the milled powder at each milling time, including the 15 h pattern; the Al-diminishing observation is made on the 15 h pattern.

method.value: mechanical alloying in a planetary ball mill

processing_steps_notes.value: Planetary ball mill (Model no. PM 400/2, Retsch) at 200 rpm; ball-to-powder ratio 10:1; carried out in tungsten carbide (WC) vials with WC balls; toluene used as a process control reagent to avoid oxidation; milling stopped intermittently for 20 min after every 1 h to avoid overheating; 2-3 g of milled powder sampled after every 5 h (so a 15 h aliquot exists) to follow phase evolution.

source.reason: The milling conditions (mill type, speed, ball-to-powder ratio, vial/ball material, toluene PCA, intermittent stops, 5 h sampling) are given in the experimental details and define the mechanical-alloying process; the 15 h state corresponds to the aliquot taken after 15 h of milling.

type.value: mechanical processing (mechanical alloying / high-energy ball milling)

source.reason: The starting constituent element phases and their crystal structures are listed for the milled powder; at 15 h the alloying is incomplete, so residual elemental phases are still present (element peak intensities decreasing with milling time).
Mn is one of the constituent elements of the milled powder; its intense peaks are still evident up to 20 h, so it is present as a residual elemental phase at 15 h.
Ni is a constituent element; its intense peaks are still evident up to 20 h of milling, so a residual Ni elemental phase is present at 15 h.
The intensity of the Al diffraction peaks diminishes after 15 h of milling, indicating Al is being consumed by alloying but is still detectable at this state.
Si is a constituent element; it remains undissolved/trace even after 35 h, so residual elemental Si is expected at 15 h.
C is a constituent interstitial element of the starting powder; it dissolves faster than the other elements but its elemental phase is part of the milled powder constitution.

The 15 h milled powder is a partially alloyed intermediate state: XRD still shows constituent-element peaks with the Al peak diminishing, and no BCC/γ-brass solid solution has yet formed (solid solution forms after 25 h). The Figure_001 description confirms the stacked XRD series includes a 15 h pattern.

overall_structure.value: As-milled powder of the Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 HES after 15 h of milling. The XRD pattern (Fig. 1(a)) is still dominated by diffraction peaks of the constituent elements, and the intensity of the Al peak diminishes after 15 h of milling, indicating that Al has the highest alloying rate. The BCC and γ-brass-type solid-solution phases are not yet formed (they appear only after 25 h of milling), so this 15 h state is a partially alloyed (elemental) powder mixture.

source.reason: Structure description built from the phase-evolution text (drawn from the XRD series including the 15 h pattern) and the cited figure showing milled-powder patterns at 0-35 h.

unmapped_findings: The 15 h milled powder is only an intermediate milling state of the study: full Rietveld-refinement parameters (lattice parameter, phase fraction, crystallite size, microstrain, dislocation density) are reported only for the 25 h, 30 h and 35 h milled powders (Table 2), so no quantitative microstructural parameters are available for the 15 h sample specifically.
Among the constituent elements, Al shows the highest alloying rate during mechanical milling, evidenced by the diminishing intensity of the Al diffraction peaks after 15 h of milling.

No mechanical or physical property measurements were performed on the 15 h milled powder; all reported mechanical properties (microhardness 7.8 ± 0.3 GPa, elastic modulus 184 ± 5 GPa, compressive strength 2046 ± 160 MPa, ~19% compressive strain) and the density (6.49 ± 0.3 g/cc) belong to the spark-plasma-sintered pellet, not to this milling-state sample.
